name: EventEnvelope
purpose: Canonical CloudEvents 1.0 shape that normalizes id, source, type, time and payload so downstream handlers parse the same structure regardless of transport.
api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EventEnvelope:
    id: str
    source: str
    type: str
    specversion: str = '1.0'
    datacontenttype: str | None = None
    dataschema: str | None = None
    subject: str | None = None
    time: str | None = None
    data: Any = None
    extensions: dict[str, str] | None = None
invariants: Producers MUST make the tuple (source, id) unique per distinct occurrence so consumers can deduplicate.
Resending the same logical event ALWAYS reuses the original id so retries do not appear as new occurrences.
specversion MUST equal '1.0' for envelopes produced under this contract.
Extension attribute names MUST follow the same naming rules as core attributes and CANNOT collide with reserved names.
time when present SHALL be an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with no timezone offset ambiguity.
extension_contract: Add custom attributes by registering an extension name in the extensions map following CloudEvents Extension Context Attributes rules; consumers extend by composing filters on type or subject via a decorator that wraps the handler.
why_essential: Dedup, replay and audit all depend on a stable identity tuple; if each producer invents its own event shape the skill cannot compose cross transport without adapters everywhere.
alternatives_considered: Plain JSON blobs per producer which breaks dedup and forces per consumer parsing rules
AsyncAPI style schema registry coupling which pins transports earlier than needed
